summary: Multitenant DNS affinity refresh causing intermittent cross-region TLS rehandshake and p50 latency uplift
description: Issue summary: FinEdge reported intermittent increases in median (p50) request latency from eu-west clients over the last 48h. Impact: ~12% of requests show an extra 80-220ms added to p50 for short windows (~30s). Customers see spikes during normal traffic periods which correlate with occasional TLS full-handshake events and a small number of cross-region egress hops. Environment: Production, eu-west tenancy for FinEdge (enterprise). Their tenant is pinned to eu-west, but traffic sometimes shows egress to us-east for a subset of requests, followed by a TLS full-handshake. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use FinEdge API key in eu-west and issue steady 20rps text-generation requests. 2) Observe p50 over rolling 1m windows. 3) Repeat while forcing client to open new TCP connections (no keepalive) and compare. Observed behavior: intermittent p50 uplift correlated with server TLS handshake time metric and edge-proxy logs showing DNS affinity refresh events. Expected behavior: pinned residency should avoid cross-region egress and reuse TLS sessions to keep p50 stable. Logs / evidence: - edge-proxy logs (edge-aws-eu-west-1) showing "affinity-refresh: resolved to [eu-edge-1, us-edge-3]" within same request window - TLS metrics: tls_full_handshake_ms spiking to 180-240ms for affected requests - Flow logs show a subset (approx 3-5%) of requests had an extra hop to us-east for 20-120s windows - Customer network trace indicates no client-side DNS re-resolve during these windows.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:34 UTC - Amira Patel: Customer reports p50 drift; attached short perf traces and request IDs. Asking for investigation priority due to enterprise SLA.
2026-03-10 11:02 UTC - SRE channel (#support): Noted similar noisy signals in eu-west around TTL refresh times. Flagging Diego to investigate affinity refresh paths.

2026-03-10 14:43 UTC - Diego Morales: Initial hypothesis: TTL skew between our internal DNS pool and edge control plane leads to simultaneous valid answers from primary and secondary edges; client-side connection steering occasionally lands on secondary causing full TLS handshake. Reproduced in staging by simulating TTL skew.
2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Eng (edge-proxy): Started an A/B of session ticket priority change to prefer session resumption across edges. Will monitor impact on p50 for FinEdge.
investigation_notes: Summary of investigation: 1) Reproduced in staging by introducing a 5s TTL delta between primary and secondary DNS responses; resulted in 2-6% of requests being routed to secondary edge for a short window. 2) Correlated edge-proxy logs with control-plane residency refresh events; occasional race where the control plane updates affinity and an edge-level cache still returns previous mapping. 3) Observed that when a request lands on an edge that does not have an established TLS session with the request source (or when client opens a fresh TCP connection), there is a full TLS handshake that adds ~150-220ms to request time. 4) Session resumption (TLS1.3 PSK) is effective when the same edge is used; resumption fails across edges without shared session tickets. Hypotheses considered: - DNS/TTL skew across our internal resolver fleet causes brief multi-edge answers for the same tenant - Edge affinity caches not invalidated atomically during control-plane updates - Some clients open new connections frequently (browser/edge cases), amplifying the effect Temporary mitigations tried: - Disabled aggressive DNS re-resolve on a subset of edge nodes for FinEdge to reduce multi-answer windows - Deployed an edge-proxy config tweak to prefer PSK session resumption and extend session ticket TTL. Metrics after mitigations: observed reduction of affected requests from ~12% to ~4% in a canary pool. Next steps: - Implement stronger control-plane --> edge cache invalidation protocol to prevent overlapping answers during affinity change windows (engineer: Diego) - Add telemetry to track multi-edge DNS answers per tenant over time (SRE) - Roll out PSK session-ticket sharing mechanism between adjacent edges where feasible (security and infra), evaluate any cryptographic risk and compliance implications for enterprise customers. - Schedule a planned deploy to all eu-west edges during low-traffic window. Repro instructions for SRE: follow conjure/staging/affinity-ttl-sim README, run the "ttl-skew" harness and observe edge logs and handshake metrics.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied (2026-03-11): 1) Canary edge config updated to prefer TLS session resumption and increase session ticket lifetime; reduced p50 impact in canary. 2) Temporary DNS re-resolve damping applied for FinEdge tenant in eu-west. Remaining work: implement control-plane cache invalidation fix (PR open), and design PSK ticket sharing architecture for adjacent edges. No permanent rollout yet; awaiting security review and extended load testing. Follow-ups: - Diego Morales to lead PR for atomic affinity cache invalidation (linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pulls/984). - SRE to monitor canary for 72h and report any regressions. - Coordinate with FinEdge to run acceptance test next week; customer notified and set to Waiting on Customer for acceptance testing when canary completes.
